answer.policy_title: Surgery of the Hip — UnitedHealthcare Commercial and Individual Exchange Medical Policy
answer.effective_date: September 10, 2026 (as posted; this is the current publicly posted version — see note below about the version that may have actually applied on the 2026-07-31 denial date)
criteria_quotes: Coverage Rationale: 'Surgery of the hip ... is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances. For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the: InterQual® Client Defined CP: Procedures: ... Removal and Replacement, Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Hip (AQS) (Custom) - UHG; Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Hip (AQS) (Custom) - UHG. Click here to view the InterQual® criteria.'
Applicable Codes table lists CPT 27130 under the heading 'Removal and Replacement, Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Hip' — confirming this is the code family the InterQual TJR-Hip criteria govern.

Definitions section supplies the clinical thresholds UHC uses when InterQual criteria reference them: 'Disabling Pain: WOMAC pain domain of > 40'; 'Functional Disability: WOMAC functional limitation domain of > 40'; Tönnis Grade 2/3 and Outerbridge Grade III/IV describe advanced osteoarthritis/cartilage damage; 'UHC will accept three or more moderate to severe radiographic findings [joint space narrowing, osteophyte formation, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral cysts, deformity of bony end plates, thinning/loss of articular cartilage] to be sufficient to support the diagnosis of severe osteoarthritis.'
answer.appeal_deadline: 180 days from the date of the notice (2026-07-31), i.e., appeal must be received by 2027-01-27, per the denial letter itself.
answer.submission_route: The denial letter text provided does not include the actual mailing address, fax number, or portal link for filing the appeal — that information is normally printed elsewhere on the full notice (often on a separate 'Appeals' page) or on the back of the Explanation of Benefits. I could not verify it independently because it is member-specific and not published on a public UHC policy page. Standard UnitedHealthcare commercial/ACA appeal channels are: (1) online through the member portal at myuhc.com, (2) by calling the member services number on the back of the UHC ID card and asking to file a formal appeal, or (3) by mail to the appeals address printed on the denial notice/EOB. The patient should use the specific address/fax/portal instructions printed on their complete denial notice, since I cannot confirm those details were included in the excerpt reviewed.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The UHC medical policy 'Surgery of the Hip' (2026T0503KK) does not itself spell out the full step-by-step medical-necessity checklist for total hip arthroplasty (CPT 27130). Instead, it incorporates by reference the InterQual® Client Defined CP criteria sets 'Removal and Replacement, Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Hip (AQS) (Custom) - UHG' and 'Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Hip (AQS) (Custom) - UHG.' InterQual is a licensed, proprietary clinical decision-support product owned by Optum/Change Healthcare; its detailed criteria are not freely published on the open web. The patient (or, more effectively, their surgeon's office) should: (1) request the specific InterQual TJR-Hip criteria and the reviewer's written rationale/clinical worksheet from UnitedHealthcare directly — insurers are generally required to provide the specific criteria relied upon in a denial upon request, especially in an appeal; (2) ask the plan in writing (as part of the appeal) to identify exactly which criterion in that InterQual set the record failed to meet; and (3) request a copy of the full 'Surgery of the Hip' medical policy version that was in effect on 2026-07-31 (the date of denial), since the version I retrieved is dated effective 2026-09-10, which post-dates the denial — an earlier version number/date likely governed this specific determination and should be requested from UHC's appeals unit or via the provider portal.
answer.notes: 1) I located and read the actual UHC 'Surgery of the Hip' commercial/Individual Exchange medical policy (2026T0503KK) that lists CPT 27130 and states the coverage rationale. This is very likely the policy family UHC is using, but the copy I could retrieve is stamped 'Effective 09/10/2026,' which is after the notice date of 2026-07-31. UHC revises this policy periodically (I found related versions for Community Plan, Medicare Advantage, Surest, and Pennsylvania Medicaid, each with different effective dates), so an earlier-dated version of the same policy title/number series was likely the one actually applied to this member's July 2026 denial. The patient/provider should confirm the exact version and date UHC applied by requesting it directly from UHC as part of the appeal. 2) The operative clinical thresholds for CPT 27130 are not fully public: the policy defers to InterQual® proprietary criteria ('Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Hip'), which are licensed content not published in full on the open web. I quoted the portions of the public policy document that describe related clinical definitions (WOMAC pain/function scores, Tönnis and Outerbridge grading, radiographic osteoarthritis findings) because these appear in the same policy and are likely the terms InterQual's TJR-Hip criteria use, but I could not verify the exact InterQual pass/fail thresholds (e.g., minimum WOMAC score, required conservative-treatment duration) because that content sits behind Optum's licensed InterQual platform. 3) I was not able to verify the specific appeal mailing address, fax number, or portal for this member's plan; the excerpted denial notice did not include it, and it is member/plan-specific, so I have not guessed at it.

NOTICE OF ADVERSE BENEFIT DETERMINATION

Date of notice: 2026-07-31
Member: Morgan Iverson
Member ID: W702529422
Plan: UnitedHealthcare (Commercial/ACA), state of Nebraska

Dear Morgan,

We reviewed the prior authorization request submitted by your provider for the following service:

    Requested service: Total hip replacement
    Procedure code (CPT): 27130

After review, this request is DENIED. Reason for determination: the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity.

This determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. You have the right to appeal this decision. Your appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of this notice (by 2027-01-27).

Reference number: POC-1C4D453F27-72744


---

If no such document is publicly available, say so explicitly and explain how

Femoroacetabular Impingement Syndrome: Femoroacetabular Impingement (FAI) Syndrome occurs because of either (1) hip formation at birth or (2) bone overgrowth (bone spurs) around the femoral head and/or along the acetabulum , causing abnormal contact between the hip bones and preventing them from moving smoothly during activity. There are three types of FAI: Pincer: This type of impingement occurs when extra bone extends out over the normal rim of the acetabulum. The labrum can be crushed under the prominent rim of the acetabulum (i.e., radiographic evidence of FAI by imaging includes overcoverage of the femoral head by the acetabulum with resultant pistol -grip deformity or the lateral center edge angle of greater than 40°, or coxa profunda, or acetabular retroversion) (Witstein et al., 2024; Pun et al., 2015). Cam: In Cam-type impingement, the femoral head is not round and cannot rotate smoothly inside the acetabulum. A bone spur forms on the edge of the femoral head that grinds the cartilage inside the acetabulum (i.e., radiographic evidence of FAI by imaging includes the loss of sphericity of the femoral head, with resultant bony prominence, or an alpha angle of greater than 50°) (Witstein et al., 2024; Pun et al., 2015). Combined (Mixed): Combined impingement means that both the Pincer and Cam types are present (Witstein et al., 2024). The HOOS consists of 43 questions in five subscales : pain, symptoms, function in daily living, function in sport and recreation, and hip-related quality of life (Nilsdotter et al., 2011). International Hip Outcome Tool (iHOT-33): A reference instrument among the patient-reported outcome measures to assess people with hip disorders, including FAI Syndrome. Outerbridge Grades: Grade 0: Normal Grade I: Cartilage with softening and swelling Grade II: Partial-thickness defect with fissures on the surface that do not reach subchondral bone or exceed 1.5 cm in diameter Grade III: Fissuring to the level of subchondral bone in an area with a diameter of more than 1.5 cm Grade IV: Exposed subchondral bone head (Slattery and Kweon, 2018) Radiographic Findings of Osteoarthritis: Narrowing of joint space, osteophyte formation, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral cysts, deformity of bony end plates, and thinning or complete loss of articular cartilage (American College of Radiology, 2025).
